placements.title: Verification Against Reference Data Extends Trust Across the Full Operating Range
placements.theme: An instrument's calibration is only trustworthy once it has been checked against a known reference and shown to hold across the entire range it will be used in, not just the point it was tuned at.
placements.why: The segment reports the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration (88.4 MHz) checked against June reference plates and confirmed to hold across the full observing band. The specific frequency and reference-plate check are one-time facts; the durable subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding is the theme that verification-against-reference is what makes a calibration trustworthy across its whole range. 'Calibration' is the exact-fit organizational stratum this observatory-calibration theme nests under.
